cities.base: Huertas or the streets between Sol and the Prado: you walk to all three galleries, Retiro and La Latina, and the Chamartín train north is one metro ride.
cities.name: Madrid

cities.base: Do not sleep here; the 08:50 Avant from Atocha has you on the hill by 09:45 and the last train back is late enough for dinner in Madrid.
cities.name: Toledo

cities.base: Gros, across the river from the Parte Vieja: five minutes to the pintxo bars, quieter at night, Zurriola beach at the door, and cheaper than the old town or the Centro.
cities.name: San Sebastián

cities.base: The Ensanche around Plaza Moyúa: fifteen minutes on foot to the Guggenheim one way and the Casco Viejo the other, and the bus station and metro are close.
cities.name: Bilbao

cities.base: The old town around Plaza de la Paz: the Barrio de la Estación cellars are a 15-minute walk down the hill, so you can taste all afternoon without a car or a driver.
cities.name: Haro

cities.base: Visit from Haro with a hire car or a booked driver; it is 30 minutes and there is no useful bus, and after three tastings nobody should be driving.
cities.name: Rioja Alavesa (Laguardia and Elciego)

places.name: Museo del Prado
places.note: Open daily; Velázquez, Goya and Bosch are the reason, and the free last two hours (18:00 to 20:00, 17:00 to 19:00 Sundays) are a queue and a crush, so pay 15 euros and go at opening.

places.name: Museo Reina Sofía
places.note: Closed Tuesdays and only open until 14:30 on Sundays; free from 19:00 to 21:00 and Sunday 12:30 to 14:30, and Guernica in the evening window is the best free hour in Madrid.

places.name: Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza
places.note: The private collection that fills in what the Prado skips, Impressionists to Hopper; free on Mondays 12:00 to 16:00, which is also the only Monday window it opens, and Saturdays run to 23:00.

places.name: Parque del Retiro and the Palacio de Cristal
places.note: The city's park, ten minutes behind the Prado; the glass palace and the boating lake are the two points, and it is where you recover from the galleries, not a destination.

places.name: Palacio Real
places.note: Bigger than Versailles and mostly empty rooms; the armoury and the view over the Casa de Campo from the courtyard are the good bits, and it shuts for state events without much warning.

places.name: Casa Revuelta
places.note: Standing-room taberna off Plaza Mayor for one thing, battered salt cod tajadas with a caña; closed Mondays, evening service Tuesday to Saturday only, and Sunday at 13:00 it is wall to wall Rastro crowd.

places.name: Bodega de la Ardosa
places.note: 1892 bar on Calle Colón with vermouth on tap, a runny tortilla and salmorejo; you duck under the bar to reach the back room, and it fills by 21:00.

places.name: Casa Dani, Mercado de la Paz
places.note: A market bar in Salamanca with the tortilla most madrileños vote best in the city and a menú del día around 15 euros; no reservations, closed Sundays, and the queue at 14:00 on a Saturday is 30 minutes.

places.name: Malacatín (cocido)
places.note: Cocido madrileño in three courses, broth then chickpeas then the meats, since 1895, lunch only and closed Sundays; book, eat nothing before, and plan nothing after.

places.name: Cava Baja tapas crawl
places.note: One street of tabernas from Casa Lucio (huevos rotos, book ahead, closed Saturday lunch and August) down to Taberna Tempranillo for wine by the glass; it is Madrid's version of the pintxo crawl and it starts at 21:00, not 19:00.

places.name: Mercado de San Miguel
places.note: A pretty iron hall that stopped being a market years ago; 4 euro croquetas and no seats, and every stall is a tourist-priced version of something better two streets away at Casa Revuelta.

places.name: El Rastro
places.note: Sunday-only flea market down Ribera de Curtidores; the stalls are mostly junk, the point is the crowd and the vermouth in the bars after, and watch your pockets.

places.name: Toledo Cathedral
places.note: One of the great Gothic cathedrals, with a sacristy of El Grecos and the Transparente; opens at 14:00 on Sundays, so do it first on any other day.

places.name: Santo Tomé (The Burial of the Count of Orgaz)
places.note: One room, one painting, El Greco's best; 3.50 euros, ten minutes if you are early and thirty behind a coach group at midday.

places.name: Sinagoga del Tránsito and Sephardic Museum
places.note: A 14th-century synagogue with Mudéjar plasterwork and the Sephardic story told well; closed Mondays, winter closing is 16:00, free Saturday afternoon and Sunday.

places.name: Monasterio de San Juan de los Reyes
places.note: The cloister is the best in Toledo and the chains on the outside wall were Christian prisoners' from Granada; winter closing is 17:45.

places.name: Alcázar and Museo del Ejército
places.note: The fortress on top of the hill, rebuilt after the Civil War siege, now the army museum; closed Mondays, free Sundays, and more interesting for the building and the Civil War rooms than the weapons.

places.name: Mezquita del Cristo de la Luz
places.note: A tiny mosque from 999 turned chapel, the oldest building in the city and the first thing you pass coming up from the escalators; ten minutes and worth it.

places.name: Mirador del Valle
places.note: The postcard of Toledo across the Tagus, the El Greco view; take the 71 bus or a taxi up (3 euros) rather than walking the road, and go late afternoon when the light is on the town.

places.name: Puente de San Martín and the river walk
places.note: The medieval bridge below the Judería, then the Senda Ecológica path along the gorge; quiet, flat, and the way to see the walls from below without a bus.

places.name: Bar Ludeña (carcamusas)
places.note: The bar that invented carcamusas, the pork and pea stew Toledo eats with bread and a beer, in a plaza off Zocodover; closed Wednesdays, and go to the bar rather than the terrace.

places.name: Alfileritos 24
places.note: A 15th-century house with a glass roof over the patio, venison and partridge done lightly; the bar upstairs does a 18 euro menú, the dining room is the proper lunch, book for 14:30.

places.name: Confitería Santo Tomé (mazapán)
places.note: Marzipan has been made in Toledo since the convents; this 1856 shop on Zocodover is the one to buy from, and the anguila (the eel-shaped loaf) travels.

places.name: Bar Nestor
places.note: Two tortillas a day, one at 13:00 and one at 20:00, 16 slices each; put your name on the list at the bar by 12:00 or 19:00, and if you miss it the tomato salad with salt and oil and the txuleta by weight are the real reason to come; closed Mondays and Sunday night.

places.name: Ganbara
places.note: The bar with the mountain of wild mushrooms on the counter, grilled with an egg yolk to order for about 18 euros; closed Sundays and Mondays, and it is at its best from October when the ceps come in.

places.name: Borda Berri
places.note: No pintxos on the bar, everything cooked to order from the chalkboard: the Idiazabal risotto and the beef cheek in wine are the two, at about 5 euros each; closed Monday and Tuesday, and breaks 15:30 to 19:30.

places.name: La Cuchara de San Telmo
places.note: A slot of a bar by San Telmo with the cochinillo (crackled suckling pig) and the foie with apple; the pig runs out around 21:00, closed Mondays and Tuesday lunch, and the crowd outside the door is part of it.

places.name: Bar Txepetxa
places.note: Marinated anchovies only, a dozen toppings, the spider crab cream is the one; closed Mondays and Sunday night, and it takes a break mid afternoon like everyone else.

places.name: La Viña (the cheesecake)
places.note: The Basque burnt cheesecake the world copied, still 6 euros a slice and still better here; it is the last stop of the crawl, not a place to sit, and it is closed Mondays.

places.name: Bar Bergara
places.note: The best cold pintxo counter in Gros, across the river from the crowds; the txalupa (mushroom and prawn gratin) has won prizes since 1987, and it is the answer to lunch on a Parte Vieja Monday.

places.name: Monte Urgull
places.note: The headland above the old town, 20 minutes up through the old fort to the Christ statue with the whole bay below; free, and the walk round the seaward side past the cemetery is the quiet part.

places.name: La Concha promenade
places.note: The white railing curve from the town hall to Ondarreta, a mile and a half of sand at low tide; swimmable June to September, walkable at any time, and the sunset from the Ondarreta end is the one.

places.name: Monte Igueldo funicular
places.note: The 1912 wooden funicular for 5.50 euros return, and the view of the bay from the top is the best in the city; the amusement park is a rusted 1950s thing you can ignore, and closing time moves with the season, earlier in winter.

places.name: Peine del Viento
places.note: Chillida's three iron combs bolted into the rocks at the end of the bay, with blowholes in the paving that fire when the swell is up; go at high tide in a westerly and it is a different place.

places.name: Sidrería Petritegi, Astigarraga
places.note: The biggest of the Astigarraga cider houses and the easiest to book, 40 to 45 euros for the fixed menu with cider from the barrel; lunch Tuesday to Sunday 13:00 to 15:00, dinner Tuesday to Saturday, 20 minutes by taxi from Gros.

places.name: Guggenheim Bilbao
places.note: 18 euros with audio guide; the building and Serra's steel spirals are the permanent point, the shows change; closed Mondays outside summer and Easter, and buy the timed ticket online the day before.

places.name: Museo de Bellas Artes
places.note: The better collection in Bilbao, Zurbarán to Bacon, in Foster's extension that fully reopens on 6 October 2026 after a five-week shut; closed Tuesdays, Sunday to 15:00, and the price after reopening was not fixed at time of writing.

places.name: Gure Toki, Plaza Nueva
places.note: The best of the Plaza Nueva bars, low-temperature egg with truffle and a proper squid-ink croqueta at 3 to 5 euros; closed Mondays, Sunday to 16:00, and on Sunday morning the plaza is a flea market.

places.name: Rio-Oja
places.note: Cazuelas on the bar and no menu: red beans, tripe, snails, cod in pil-pil, a plate for 6 to 8 euros with bread and a glass; closed Sundays and the mid afternoon, and it is the cheapest honest lunch in the old town.

places.name: Xukela
places.note: Calle del Perro bar, red walls and a long counter of cold pintxos, the foie on toast under 4 euros; open daily, Sunday to 16:00, and it is where the old town drinks after 21:00.

places.name: Mercado de la Ribera
places.note: A 1929 art deco market hall on the river, the fish counters are the real thing before 12:00; the gastro bars at the end stay open later and are fine, not special, and the market side shuts Sundays.

places.name: Casa Rufo
places.note: A grocery shop with tables in the back and a txuleta for two grilled properly, plus a wall of Rioja at shop prices; book, closed Sundays, and go for the steak, not the starters.

places.name: La Viña del Ensanche
places.note: Since 1927, and the reason to go is the Joselito ham carved to order and the croquetas, with a glass of Rioja at the bar; closed Sundays, and busy with office lunch from 14:00.

places.name: Artxanda funicular
places.note: Three minutes up for about 2.50 euros each way, and the whole valley with the Guggenheim's roof is laid out; go at dusk when the titanium goes orange, and the park at the top has a bar.

places.name: Riverside walk, Zubizuri to the Guggenheim
places.note: Calatrava's white bridge (slippery when wet, which is always), then along the Nervión past the Iberdrola tower to Puppy; this is the route from the Casco Viejo to the museum and it is better than the tram.

places.name: Azkuna Zentroa
places.note: A 1909 wine warehouse gutted by Philippe Starck into a cultural centre held up on 43 different columns, with a glass-bottomed pool overhead; free, ten minutes, and a good wet-weather coffee stop.

places.name: Puente Colgante (Vizcaya Bridge)
places.note: The world's oldest transporter bridge, 1893, a UNESCO site 20 minutes by metro to Areeta; the gondola crossing is under 1 euro and runs all night, the walkway 50 metres up is about 10 euros and closes earlier in winter.

places.name: López de Heredia Viña Tondonia
places.note: The 1877 cellars with mould on every wall and a Zaha Hadid tasting pavilion, wines released a decade late and cheaper than they should be; visits are by email only (visitas@tondonia.com), Monday to Saturday, book weeks ahead, no tours during harvest, and the fee is confirmed when you book.

places.name: Bodegas Muga
places.note: The most visitor-ready house on the street, 25 euros for 90 minutes and three wines, with its own cooperage still making barrels; Monday to Saturday by reservation, and the easiest of the seven to actually get into.

places.name: CVNE
places.note: 1879, with an Eiffel-company steel roof over the barrel hall and the Imperial Gran Reserva that people know; booked online, 15 to 35 euros depending on the wines, and a good second visit after López de Heredia.

places.name: Gómez Cruzado
places.note: The smallest of the station houses, 1886, and the one where the winemaker is likely to be the person pouring; book by email a few days ahead, and it is the least crowded visit on the street.

places.name: Bodegas Roda
places.note: The modern one, 1987, with a terrace over the Ebro bend and a serious tasting; pricier at 20 to 50 euros and it shows in the glasses, book online, closed Sundays.

places.name: La Herradura wine bars
places.note: The horseshoe of streets behind Plaza de la Paz where Haro drinks: a crianza is 2 euros a glass, the pintxos are simpler than San Sebastián's, and Thursday to Saturday nights are the ones with people in them.

places.name: Terete
places.note: Roast lamb from a wood oven since 1877, on shared long tables with a house Rioja from their own cellar; closed Mondays and Sunday nights, book for Sunday lunch, and order the lamb and the asparagus and nothing else.

places.name: Plaza de la Paz and the old town
places.note: A glass-balconied square, the Santo Tomás church with a carved Plateresque doorway, and the 19th-century wine money in the palacios around it; half an hour, and the walk down to the station district from here is 15 minutes.

places.name: Vivanco Museo de la Cultura del Vino, Briones
places.note: The best wine museum anywhere, 8 km from Haro (10 minutes by taxi), with Picasso ceramics and 5,000 years of corkscrews; closed Mondays, Saturday to 20:00, and it needs two hours or it is not worth going.

places.name: Briones village
places.note: A stone hill village above the Ebro with a walled top and a view across the vines to the Sierra de Cantabria; pair it with Vivanco below it, and the bar on the square does a decent bocadillo.

places.name: Laguardia walled town walk
places.note: A medieval hill town where cars are banned because the ground underneath is hollow with 300 cellars; walk the ramparts, the two gates and the main street, and get here before the tour buses at 11:00.

places.name: Santa María de los Reyes portico
places.note: A 14th-century Gothic doorway that kept its original paint because a later wall sealed it in; seen only on the tourist office's guided slot, so book the time at the office on the main street when you arrive.

places.name: Bodega El Fabulista
places.note: One of the underground cellars beneath the town, 7 metres down under the fabulist Samaniego's house, still making wine by carbonic maceration; about 10 euros for the tour and two glasses, visits at set times, and it is the one bodega you can do on foot.

places.name: Bodegas Ysios
places.note: Calatrava's wave-roofed winery under the Sierra de Cantabria, 2 km north of Laguardia; the building outdoes the wine, 15 to 30 euros, book online a week ahead, and the outside can be photographed from the road for free.

places.name: Marqués de Riscal, Elciego
places.note: Gehry's titanium ribbons over an 1858 bodega, open daily; the 30 euro 90-minute visit gets you the old cellar, three wines and a look at the hotel, and it is the most booked-out visit in Rioja, so reserve a week or more ahead.

places.name: Bodegas Baigorri, Samaniego
places.note: A glass box on the surface and seven gravity-fed floors underground, and the restaurant at the bottom does the best winery lunch in the region at about 60 euros with wine; on the road between Haro and Laguardia, so it is the natural lunch stop.

places.name: Remírez de Ganuza, Samaniego
places.note: A small serious estate that sorts every bunch by hand and cuts the tips off; 20 to 40 euros, by appointment only and closed Sundays, and it is for people who care about the wine rather than the building.

places.name: Balcón de la Rioja
places.note: A lay-by on the A-2124 at the top of the Herrera pass, 1,100 metres up, with the whole Rioja plain below; 15 minutes' drive north of Laguardia and the only reason to leave the vineyards, so do it on the way to or from Vitoria if you go that way.

places.name: San Vicente de la Sonsierra
places.note: A castle village on a crag over the Ebro halfway between Haro and Laguardia; climb to the church and the ruined keep for the river view, and it costs nothing and takes 45 minutes on the way through.

places.name: Amelibia, Laguardia
places.note: A dining room on the town wall with the vineyards under the window, Riojan cooking done cleanly and a 35 euro menu that includes the wine; lunch mostly, closed Mondays, book because there are 30 seats.

outings.why: All three galleries sit on the Paseo del Prado; the hard part is stamina, so do Prado in the morning, Thyssen after lunch and the Reina Sofía in its free window from 19:00, and skip it on Tuesdays when it is shut.
outings.name: The Prado, the Reina Sofía and the Thyssen

outings.why: 33 minutes on the train, then a whole day on a steep hill city: the cathedral, El Greco's Burial at Santo Tomé, the synagogues and the mirador across the Tagus; the climb and the cobbles are the work.
outings.name: Toledo on the Avant train
outings.season: all year, brutal in July and August
outings.fallback: Cathedral, Santo Tomé and lunch, back on the 16:25.

outings.why: 27 minutes on the Avant to Segovia-Guiomar then a bus into town; the Roman aqueduct is the reason, the Alcázar is fine, and roast suckling pig at lunch is the meal, at about 30 dollars a head; do this or Toledo, not both.
outings.name: Segovia: the aqueduct, the Alcázar and cochinillo

outings.why: One or two pintxos and one drink per bar, five or six bars, standing; start at 19:30 when the hot kitchens open, and do it Wednesday to Saturday because Ganbara, Borda Berri and Nestor are shut on Mondays and several on Sundays too.
outings.name: The Parte Vieja pintxo crawl
outings.fallback: Bar Sport and Atari, which open daily.

outings.why: A cider house in Astigarraga, 20 minutes by taxi or bus: cod omelette, fried cod, a txuleta shared by two, cheese with quince, and unlimited cider you pour yourself from the barrel when someone shouts txotx; the set menu is about 45 dollars
outings.name: Txotx at Petritegi
outings.season: all year; barrel season January to April is the real thing
outings.fallback: The same menu at dinner, Tuesday to Saturday.

outings.why: Walk the whole curve of La Concha to Ondarreta, see Chillida's Peine del Viento at the end, ride the 1912 funicular up Igueldo for the view back, then walk down; flat except the hill.
outings.name: Igueldo, the Peine del Viento and La Concha
outings.fallback: La Concha promenade and a coffee at Ondarreta.

outings.why: Two hours inside, an hour outside with Puppy and the spider, then the river walk under the Calatrava bridge to the Casco Viejo for a late lunch; shut on Mondays outside summer.
outings.name: The Guggenheim and the riverside
outings.fallback: Bellas Artes on a Guggenheim Monday, though Bellas Artes shuts Tuesdays.

outings.why: Metro to Areeta, ride the 1893 transporter bridge gondola across the river for under a dollar, walk the top walkway for 10 dollars, then along the old port at Getxo; it is a half day and good on a Monday when the museums are shut.
outings.name: The Puente Colgante and Getxo
outings.fallback: Gondola only and pintxos in Portugalete.

outings.why: Seven historic Rioja houses on one street below Haro: López de Heredia, Muga, CVNE, Gómez Cruzado, Roda, Bilbaínas, La Rioja Alta; two booked visits is the limit for one day, every one is appointment-only, and López de Heredia has to be ema
outings.name: The Barrio de la Estación
outings.season: all year except harvest, late September to mid October, when
outings.fallback: Muga, which is the easiest to book, then wine on La Herradura.

outings.why: The walled hill town of Laguardia, Calatrava's Ysios and Gehry's Marqués de Riscal in one loop under the Sierra de Cantabria; it needs a car or a driver and a designated non-drinker, and the bodegas need booking a week ahead.
outings.name: Rioja Alavesa by car: Laguardia, Ysios and Riscal
outings.season: all year; vines are bare December to April
outings.fallback: Laguardia and one underground bodega there, no driving between wineries.

destination.name: Madrid and the Basque north
destination.pitch: Three big-gallery days in Madrid with Toledo tacked on, then the train north to eat: San Sebastián's pintxo bars done bar by bar, Bilbao for the Guggenheim and a quieter old town, and Haro so the Rioja cellars are a walk and not a drive.
destination.caveat: The north is wet and grey at any time of year and the good pintxo bars close on Mondays and often Sundays too, so a badly placed weekend can put you in San Sebastián on the two days it does not work. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Madrid is a proper capital that eats at 22:00, and San Sebastián and Bilbao are two of the best small cities in Europe to walk.
because.food: Pintxos in the Parte Vieja, cider-house txotx in Astigarraga, Madrid cocido at lunch and Rioja tasted in the cellar it was made in: this is the strongest eating region in Spain.
because.nature: La Concha and the Urgull headland give San Sebastián a real coastline, and the Rioja vineyards under the Sierra de Cantabria are the one landscape day.
because.culture: The Prado, Reina Sofía and Thyssen are three of Europe's top galleries within a ten-minute walk of each other, and Toledo is the whole medieval Spanish story in one hill.
because.adventure: Very little: a coastal hill walk, a funicular and a cellar ladder is as hard as it gets.
because.relaxation: Afternoons on La Concha and long Rioja lunches are slow by design, if you let the museum days go.
because.exploration: Toledo, Segovia, Haro's station district and the Rioja Alavesa hill villages are each a full day that most visitors never do.
